blocks.text: INN NEWS - Free Bergizi Eating Program Hourted President Prabowo Subianto and Vice President Gibran Ranakuming Raka has become a very warm topic in Indonesia, over with a recent premiere.
With the promise of giving free lunch to school kids, it's meant to address the problem of malnutrition and stunting and improve education quality.
However, his implementation requires strict supervision because of the number of challenges and problems that have been seen in the early stages.
Unhappiness Menu

One of the main challenges of this program is the unhappiness of menus given to children in different areas. An uneven food spread could occur because of complex logistics in Indonesia with diverse geographical conditions.
Some cases have been reported where the menus that children receive are different from one area to another, not only in terms of food type but also its quality and quantity.
For example, in urban areas it might be a more variable menu than in remote areas, which could result in malnutrition between children.
Food and Child Liquor
Food tastes are also an important issue. Children tend to have strong palate preferences, and if food is served not according to their taste, a lot of food will be wasted.

There's a report on social media about children who don't eat food that is provided because it doesn't fit their liking, which certainly doesn't meet the purpose of this program, which is to provide enough nutrition.
Milk Supplies
The absence of milk on the free lunch menu also became a spotlight. Milk is an important source of calcium for the growth of bones and teeth of children.
However, from some sources it is known that not all children get milk in this program, either due to limited availability or because of logistics problems in distribution.
It's come to serious attention, given that milk is an integral part of a healthy diet for children.
Observer Comment
Social Observation and public policy have given critical input to the execution of this program.
Muhammad Gumarang, as one observer, emphasized the importance of government to detail the technical execution, including budgets, distribution and quality of food.
He highlighted that without careful planning, the program could be a burden to APBN and ineffective in achieving its goal.

Other observers, such as Numal Idrus from Hasanuddin University, support the formation of a special ministry to handle this program, which he thinks will provide certainty and effectiveness in execution.
However, he also warned that if not managed properly, the program could be a new source of corruption.
